chapter_context.significance: Proof-of-concept implementation — first time append-only ledger principle became executable code

design_philosophy.purpose: Single-file ledger + Merkle + SHA-256 + self-test. Ingest raw dumps, hash them, maintain Merkle-style head, export + self-test.
design_principles: Zero external dependencies — single file, Node.js built-ins or browser Web Crypto API only
Graceful degradation — three-tier hash fallback: Node.js crypto → Web Crypto API → weak hash
Self-verifying — built-in verify() proves chain integrity at any time
Self-testing — selfTest() demonstrates both clean verification and tamper detection
Portable — runs in Node.js CLI or browser environment without modification

canon_guardrails.implementation: append() method only — no delete() or update() exists
sha256Hex() with Node.js crypto + browser fallback
exportState() — explicit export, never pretends permanent

functions.name: stableCanonicalJSON(value)
functions.purpose: Deterministic JSON output regardless of key insertion order

functions.name: merklePairHash(left, right)

layers.name: PhoenixMegaLedger class
layers.significance: Heart of Stage 3 — implements Axiom 1 (Ledger is Law) as code

methods.name: append(rawText, meta)
steps: Validates raw text exists and is non-empty
Computes SHA-256 of raw text content
Creates envelope: {nonce, timestamp, rawLen, rawSha256, prevHash}
Hashes envelope to produce event hash
Chains to previous event via prevHash
Trims oldest events if buffer exceeds maxEvents

methods.name: verify()
checks: computes Merkle root over all verified hashes

failure_modes.cause: recomputed hash differs — envelope data tampered

methods.returns: {ok, headHash, height, merkleRoot, count} or {ok: false, reason, at}

methods.name: exportState()
methods.purpose: Runs full verification, returns complete ledger state including Merkle root
methods.guardrail: Implements 'no fake persistence' — state explicitly exported, never assumed permanent

layers.name: Self-Test Harness

tests.name: Clean test
tests.steps: Append 3 events → verify → should return {ok: true}

tests.name: Corrupt test
tests.steps: Copy events, tamper event[1] prevHash → verify → should return {ok: false, reason: CHAINBREAK}

layers.significance: System testing itself — direct implementation of SYF Truth Protocol at code level

commands.action: Append event and print hash proof
